# JackedIN

> The SSH, Telnet and serial terminal built for AI agents. It waits for the device prompt and reads the complete output. A stdio MCP server and a token-protected localhost API (off by default) hook it into Cursor, Claude Desktop, and other MCP clients.

Official website: https://getjackedin.com/
The current product page is served at https://getpathprobe.com/jackedin/ (getjackedin.com redirects there).
Support: service@getpathprobe.com

JackedIN runs the same engine from the window, the CLI, Python, Ansible, and MCP. `jackedin exec` (and the MCP `exec` tool) reads the command list first, waits until the device prompt returns, pages through `--More--` and similar markers, and can print JSON (`--json` or `--output json`, or `JACKEDIN_JSON=1`). Use it instead of piping into `jackedin connect`. Pacing flags are `--line-delay`, `--char-delay`, and `--wait-for-echo`. `--prompt REGEX` replaces the detected prompt; `--vendor NAME` forces a profile. Built-in profiles for Junos, Cisco IOS/NX-OS, Arista, Nokia, MikroTik and more.

The MCP server is `jackedin mcp` (stdio). It dials 127.0.0.1 only. Leave the app open with the local API turned on, or run `jackedin headless`. The local API is off by default, listens on 127.0.0.1 only (port 47321 unless changed), and requires a Bearer token (`JACKEDIN_API_TOKEN` or the token saved in Settings). Tools: list_sessions, open_session, send_session, exec, send_break, read_session, close_session, wait_for_output, scan_ports, ping_host, trace_host, read_events. A 72-hour full trial unlocks every feature; after that a $19 one-time license is required (one license, one computer).

Since 1.2.2: In AI sessions (MCP and the local API), show-type commands run freely; a command that changes something runs only after a person approves it in the window or on the jackedin headless terminal; a denial or 60 seconds with no answer means it is not sent; the agent can never approve itself. jackedin plink accepts the common PuTTY plink flags.

Only use JackedIN on devices you own or are allowed to manage. Current release is JackedIN 1.2.3. There is no macOS build yet.

New in 1.2.3: every shipped program (jackedin.exe, jackedin.com, jackedin, jackedin-cli) checks itself against a signed integrity manifest at startup; a modified copy is refused with "This copy is damaged or has been modified; re-download from getpathprobe.com." Existing licenses are unaffected. Standalone Linux binaries ship with a <name>.integrity file to keep beside them.

## Docs

- [Product page and download](https://getpathprobe.com/jackedin/): Windows, Linux, and Raspberry Pi (arm64) builds, 72-hour trial, pricing
- [Using JackedIN with AI agents](https://getpathprobe.com/jackedin/ai-agents/): MCP setup, verified exec, and human approval before any change
- [Coming from plink?](https://getpathprobe.com/jackedin/ai-agents/#from-plink): jackedin exec waits for the device prompt; plink sends a command file or stdin in one block and remains a better tiny, free SSH transport for Git
- [User's guide (Markdown)](https://github.com/getpathprobe/jackedin-releases/releases/download/v1.2.3/JackedIN-Users-Guide.md): CLI, verified exec, local API, and MCP
- [User's guide (HTML)](https://github.com/getpathprobe/jackedin-releases/releases/download/v1.2.3/JackedIN-Users-Guide.html): same guide as HTML
- [JackedIN 1.2.3 release](https://github.com/getpathprobe/jackedin-releases/releases/tag/v1.2.3): release notes, installers, packages, and standalone binaries
- [SHA256SUMS (JackedIN 1.2.3)](https://github.com/getpathprobe/jackedin-releases/releases/download/v1.2.3/SHA256SUMS): checksums for every file in that release
- [Python guide](https://github.com/getpathprobe/jackedin-releases/blob/main/JackedIN-Python-Guide.md): free `jackedin` and `nornir-jackedin` packages (the app trial or a license is still required)
- [Site-wide llms.txt](https://getpathprobe.com/llms.txt): JackedIN and PathProbe index
